title: Localizing away from the zerodivisors of a fibre module: the spectrum is semi-local on the associated primes
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'Localization and universally injective maps'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the spectrum of the localisation Sigma^{-1}S where Sigma is the set of elements that are not zerodivisors on the fibre module Nbar = N/m_R N: it must be shown semi-local, with primes contained in an associated prime of Nbar, and with maximal ideals in bijection with the associated primes of Nbar over Sbar (statement lines 1792-1797). The argument is a chain of identifications rather than a construction, but the identification Sigma = S minus the union of the associated primes is what makes the localisation computable, and the two hypotheses that Sbar is Noetherian and Nbar finite over Sbar are both needed to make that union finite (proof lines 1801-1814). Every step is a citation of a standard commutative-algebra lemma, so the claim is H2.
